assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening of neutrino astronomy: the 2013 detection of a diffuse flux of TeV-PeV astrophysical neutrinos in a cubic-kilometre Antarctic ice detector, later supported by the 2018 TXS 0506+056 association and the 2023 Galactic-plane evidence. It is an original instrument-driven discovery with a clear scientific consequence: a new window on cosmic-ray accelerators. As an astroparticle experimentalist I weigh the instrumental achievement heavily.
assessment.attribution: The supplied credit lists only Francis Halzen, the concept's driving proponent and long-time lead of the collaboration. IceCube is a large collaboration whose AMANDA predecessor, the detector construction and the analysis teams all contributed decisively, so a single-laureate prize would need justification and a second or third name might be warranted but none is supplied.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation exists from multiple analyses and later source-association evidence, and the diffuse flux has been reproduced across channels. Source identification remains incomplete, so the astrophysics is still maturing, but the discovery of the flux itself is well established and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether a single named laureate fairly represents a collaboration discovery.
Origin of the diffuse flux is still largely unresolved, and individual source associations remain statistically modest.
I am relying on my own recollection of the IceCube results and have not independently verified them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and have transformed precision timekeeping, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. The idea is original, conceptually clean and experimentally decisive.
assessment.attribution: A natural two-laureate configuration: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and demonstrated it, and Ye led the work that brought lattice clocks to record accuracy and stability. Other groups (for example Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow) contributed, so some credit is left outside, but this is a coherent core.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and independently reproduced by numerous laboratories worldwide. Timing is plausible given the ongoing discussion of redefining the SI second, though that redefinition has not yet happened.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior frequency-metrology recognition (optical frequency combs, 2005) could be argued by some.
Whether the redefinition of the second should be awaited before recognition is a matter of judgement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of X-ray, optical and radio afterglows of gamma-ray bursts, first with BeppoSAX in 1997, settled the long-standing question of their distance and showed they are cosmological, extremely energetic events. This solved a 30-year puzzle and underpins GRB physics, links to supernovae and compact-object mergers, and multi-messenger astronomy. Space instrumentation led directly to the result, which resonates with my own field.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX wide-field and narrow-field X-ray observations that provided the accurate positions; Kulkarni's group secured the redshift and the radio and optical follow-up that established the distance scale. Other decisive contributors exist: Jan van Paradijs (deceased) led the optical identification, and Paczynski, Rees and Meszaros contributed to the theory. The three supplied names form a defensible but imperfect configuration.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed over more than two decades by Swift, Fermi and ground-based follow-up. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Credit is disputed or incomplete because of the deceased contributor and the many groups involved in the rapid follow-up.
Whether the committee would prefer to recognise theory of the fireball model alongside observation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene launched the field of moire quantum materials, with flat bands, correlated insulators and unconventional superconductivity in a tunable platform. The 2011 Bistritzer-MacDonald theory predicted the magic angle and the 2018 experiments realised it. Originality and impact on condensed-matter physics are very high.
assessment.attribution: A theory-plus-experiment pairing is natural: MacDonald (with Bistritzer) for the prediction of flat bands at the magic angle, and Jarillo-Herrero for the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity. Eva Andrei and Rafi Bistritzer have strong claims and the three-name limit forces hard choices; I regard this allocation as unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Many groups have reproduced the main phenomena, but the interpretation of the superconducting pairing mechanism and sample-to-sample variation remain unsettled. Recognition would be timely but somewhat early for the mechanism.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved.
Allocation among MacDonald, Bistritzer, Jarillo-Herrero and Andrei is contested.
This is outside my own expertise, so my assessment is more reliant on general knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of a surprisingly large theta13 completed the three-flavour mixing picture and opened the path to measuring CP violation in the lepton sector. It was a precision reactor experiment with a clean, decisive result obtained in 2012, and I value the instrument design and systematic control.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang and Luk as spokespersons) and RENO and Double Chooz measured theta13 with reactor antineutrinos, while T2K (Nishikawa) provided early appearance indications. Because several collaborations contributed, a prize would need to select among them, and the supplied names do not cover RENO or Double Chooz. I therefore propose the two Daya Bay leaders but regard attribution as contested.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by multiple experiments and by accelerator appearance data; the value is now a precision parameter. Neutrino oscillations were recognised in 2015, so a follow-on prize is plausible but not urgent.
uncertainties: Competition between Daya Bay, RENO, Double Chooz and T2K for primary credit.
Possible view that the result is a measurement of a parameter within an already awarded framework.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar timing arrays gave the 2023 evidence for a nanohertz stochastic gravitational-wave background, probably from supermassive black-hole binaries, opening a new gravitational-wave band. The technique and decades-long timing campaigns are remarkable.
assessment.attribution: The result came from several collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA/InPTA, PPTA, CPTA), and the supplied three names cannot cover the field's founders (Detweiler, Hellings-Downs, Foster-Backer) or all collaborations. Credit allocation is the central problem.
assessment.maturity: The evidence is only at roughly 3-4 sigma for the characteristic spatial correlation, the source is unidentified, and the interpretation (binaries versus new physics) is open. Recognition now looks premature.
uncertainties: Statistical significance short of discovery level.
Source of the signal is unidentified.
Large and unresolved attribution among collaborations and founders.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations, detected in 2005 in SDSS and 2dFGRS, give a standard ruler that anchors the cosmic distance scale and dark-energy constraints. It is a clean, robust observable and a core pillar of precision cosmology.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein (SDSS luminous red galaxy detection) and Cole and Percival (2dFGRS analysis) made the key detections; theoretical prediction by Peebles and Yu, Sunyaev and Zeldovich is a further source of credit, and cosmology prizes have already recognised Peebles. A fair three-name set is supportable but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed by BOSS, eBOSS, DESI and others. Recent DESI hints on evolving dark energy are not yet settled but do not weaken the standard-ruler method.
uncertainties: Prior theoretical credit and the earlier cosmology prizes may complicate a new award.
Unclear whether the committee prefers the measurement or the dark-energy conclusions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices: the Jaksch-Zoller proposal and the Greiner-Bloch observation of the superfluid to Mott insulator transition made a controllable platform for many-body quantum physics.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (theory), Greiner and Bloch (experiment) is a reasonable trio, though Cirac and Esslinger have strong claims and the supplied list of five exceeds the three-laureate limit.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely reproduced; the field's broader goals of useful analogue simulation are still developing, and previous recognition of ultracold gases (2001) may reduce urgency.
uncertainties: Five credited people compete for three slots.
Overlap with related candidates involving Cirac and Zoller on trapped ions and Rydberg arrays.
